job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
Financial Controller | Global Manufacturing | Eastern Creek | $160,000–$180,000 + Super

Join a globally recognised organisation with a strong international presence and established operations across Australia and New Zealand. With a focus on innovation, regional growth and operational excellence, the business continues to invest in its people, systems and capabilities.
An opportunity has arisen for an experienced Financial Controller to lead the Australian finance function, working closely with local leadership and global finance stakeholders. This is a hands-on leadership role offering the opportunity to influence business performance, strengthen financial processes and drive continuous improvement.

The Position
Reporting to the local CEO and Global Finance leadership, you will oversee financial operations, provide commercial insights and ensure strong financial controls and compliance. You will lead a small finance team while partnering with the wider business to support informed decision-making and improve operational performance.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Lead budgeting, forecasting and financial planning, providing insights to support business decisions and profitability.
  • Oversee monthly financial reporting, including P&L, balance sheet, operating expenditure and key performance indicators.
  • Analyse financial results and budget variances, identifying risks and opportunities for improvement.
  • Manage cash flow, working capital, aged debtors and payment processes.
  • Oversee tax compliance, statutory reporting and external audit requirements.
  • Maintain robust financial controls, ensuring accurate and reliable reporting.
  • Lead, mentor and develop a small finance team across accounting, accounts payable and accounts receivable.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline finance processes, improve reporting and strengthen internal controls.
  • Partner with IT and key stakeholders on finance systems and process improvement initiatives.
  • Build strong relationships with local management, global finance teams, auditors, banks and external advisers.
The Candidate
You are a commercially minded finance leader who combines strong technical accounting skills with the ability to see the bigger business picture. Comfortable operating at both a strategic and hands-on level, you can translate financial information into meaningful insights and build strong relationships across the organisation.
Ideally, you will bring:
  • CA/CPA qualification and experience in financial control or senior finance leadership.
  • Experience in manufacturing, distribution or a similar operational environment.
  • Proven experience leading and developing a finance team.
  • Experience working within an international group structure and liaising with overseas head office.
  • A track record of improving processes, systems and reporting.
  • Strong analytical skills and commercial acumen, with the confidence to influence senior stakeholders.
The Benefits
  • $160,000–$180,000 + superannuation.
  • Eastern Creek location with on-site parking.
  • Opportunity to lead a broad finance function with direct influence on business performance.
  • Exposure to local executive leadership and international finance stakeholders.
  • Join an established global organisation with a focus on innovation and growth.
  • The opportunity to develop your team, improve processes and contribute to ongoing business improvement.

job.title: HR Operations Manager
job.description:
Western Sydney location | $150k  + Super + Bonus
  • Lead an established HR operations team supporting a large, national workforce
  • Take ownership of HR operations, systems, compliance and service delivery
  • Join a successful, well-established organisation offering stability, autonomy and genuine leadership opportunity
The Opportunity
Are you an experienced HR operations leader who enjoys bringing order to complexity, developing people and making things run better?
A well-established national organisation with a strong reputation is seeking an HR Operations Manager to lead its centralised HR Operations function. This role suits someone who thrives in a fast-paced, high-volume environment and enjoys balancing team leadership and process improvement with hands-on operational HR.
You’ll join a business known for its practical, down-to-earth culture. Backed by an experienced leadership team, you’ll have the autonomy to own the function and make a genuine, lasting impact.

About the Role
You’ll lead a small team and oversee the delivery of accurate, efficient and compliant HR operations across a geographically dispersed workforce.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Leading, coaching and developing an established HR Operations team, driving accountability, engagement and high performance.
  • Overseeing end-to-end HR operations, including employment contracts, on-boarding, employee changes and off-boarding.
  • Driving operational excellence, ensuring service delivery meets agreed time-frames, quality standards and business expectations.
  • Owning HR systems and processes, streamlining workflows, documenting procedures and training team members to improve efficiency and enhance the employee experience.
  • Maintaining compliance, overseeing award interpretation, employment documentation and HR governance.
  • Owning WGEA reporting and compliance obligations.
  • Managing HR reporting, including workforce data and compliance reporting.
About You
We’re looking for a confident, capable HR Operations Manager who combines strong technical knowledge with a genuine passion for people leadership and continuous improvement.
Ideally, you’ll bring:
  • Solid experience in HR Services, HR Operations or a similar team leadership role within a large, complex organisation.
  • Exposure to acquisitions, business integration's or large-scale employee on-boarding would be highly regarded.
  • Demonstrated experience leading an HR administration or shared services team within a high-volume environment.
  • Strong knowledge of employment contracts, Modern Awards, HR compliance and employee life-cycle processes.
  • Confidence working with HRIS platforms, reporting and data, including strong Excel skills.
  • A track record of improving processes, streamlining workflows, documenting procedures and developing team capability.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to build credibility with stakeholders at all levels.
Most importantly, you’re someone who takes ownership, leads by example and isn’t afraid to roll up your sleeves. You’re organised, solutions-focused and know how to bring out the best in your team while keeping the bigger picture in mind.

What’s on Offer?

  • Hybrid working arrangements

You will play an important role in supporting the sales function, ensuring customer orders are processed accurately, system information is maintained and communication between customers, sales, production, warehouse and logistics runs efficiently.

job.title: Operational Safety Manager
job.description:
Operational Safety Manager   |  Western Sydney  |  $170K to $180K + Super

The Company:

Step into a fast-growing, privately-owned operator in a highly regulated, safety-critical industry, with an evolving and expanding service offering. Safety isn't a compliance box here. It's a genuine leadership priority, backed by real authority and real investment, and our client is looking for someone who wants to help shape what safety looks like, not just maintain what already exists.

This is a newly defined Operational Safety Manager role, created because the business is ready to invest properly in safety leadership, not just fill a gap. It comes with a clear runway to a broader Head of Safety and Compliance position for the right person, giving you a real say in how the function grows from here.

The Position:

Reporting directly to the General Manager, you'll take genuine ownership of operational safety, not oversight from a distance, leading a ground-up review of current procedures with the mandate to reshape how safety works from day one.

What you'll be doing:
  • Leading a full, ground-up review of current safety procedures and driving practical improvements
  • Rebuilding and maintaining SWMS, risk assessments and safe operating procedures
  • Owning incident and near-miss investigations end to end, from first response and root cause analysis through to corrective actions and close-out
  • Building operational readiness for dangerous goods handling and storage, including training, risk assessments and emergency response procedures
  • Leading safety training, coaching and toolbox talks across drivers, plant operators and site teams
  • Driving a genuine, measurable shift in safety culture, particularly building trust and buy-in within driver and operational teams
  • Overseeing Chain of Responsibility and heavy vehicle safety at the operational level, including fatigue, loading and scheduling risk
  • Managing Return to Work and Workers Compensation cases from notification through to resolution
  • Coordinating emergency preparedness, including planning, drills, and post-incident review
  • Exercising full stop-work authority where you identify unsafe activity, backed by senior leadership
  • Partnering closely with senior operational leaders across the business to embed safety into day-to-day decision-making
  • Reporting on safety performance and trends to the General Manager, with a clear line of sight to broader compliance and business risk
The Candidate:

We're looking for someone genuinely progressive in how they think about safety, someone who sees it as a driver of performance and culture, not just a regulatory requirement. This role suits an experienced, dynamic safety leader who wants to build and shape something, not simply administer an existing system.

You'll bring:
  • Significant experience in a senior operational safety or WHS leadership role within transport, waste, logistics, industrial or another high-risk, regulated environment
  • Solid working knowledge of Chain of Responsibility, NHVR requirements, and heavy vehicle or bulk transport safety
  • A strong track record of leading incident investigations and translating findings into real, followed procedures
  • Genuine comfort operating in yards, depots and vehicles, not a desk-bound safety professional
  • The confidence to challenge unsafe practices and influence change at every level of a business, regardless of commercial pressure
  • Experience with, or strong exposure to, dangerous goods, chemical handling or petrochemical environments (highly regarded, not essential)
  • Background with a larger, structured logistics or industrial organisation is a plus, but we're just as open to a hands-on operator from a smaller business who's ready to step up
The Benefits:
  • $170,000 to $180,000 + super
  • A newly created role with genuine scope to shape safety strategy and execution from day one
  • A clear, realistic progression pathway to a Head of Safety and Compliance role
  • Full authority and senior leadership backing to make safety decisions that matter
  • Involvement in a major growth initiative: the safe expansion into dangerous goods
  • A hands-on, high-impact culture where your work is visible and valued, not lost in bureaucracy
  • The chance to build modern, practical safety systems in a business that's genuinely investing in getting it right
